title: Give each shop its own metrics, built where the shop starts

blocks.text: The shop's checkout and refund services used to count into `Metrics.getInstance()`. Now the hosting platform runs one shop per tenant, several in one JVM, and each tenant's dashboard showed every tenant's orders. The team has removed the static accessor: `Checkout` and `Refunds` take a `Metrics` in their constructors, and `Shop.start()` is where the platform builds a shop when a tenant's shop starts.

Finish the three `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Shop.java`: the two constructors and `start()`. When you're done, each running shop's dashboard (`Running.metrics()`) shows exactly what that shop's own checkout and refunds counted. About five lines in total.

cases.says: orders taken by a started shop's checkout show on that shop's metrics
a Checkout or Refunds built with a Metrics counts into that Metrics
the services of one shop share one Metrics, the one its dashboard reads
two shops started in one JVM each count only their own events

origin.section: A Static Singleton Carries One Test's State Into the Next

concepts: Building the one instance in main and passing it through constructors keeps one instance in production and lets each test build its own.
